title: ⚡ Flash Loans: Borrow $10M in One Transaction (No Collateral)
ig_caption:
Borrow $10M with ZERO collateral… in ONE transaction ⚡
Revert if you fail—profit only if it all lands.

• Step 1: TRY #1 — execute the plan (borrow + trade) within the same tx
• Step 2: 2 REVERT — if repayment conditions aren’t met, the entire transaction is undone
• Step 3: TRY #2 — run again, but this time ensure the repayment happens atomically
• Step 4: PROFIT — once the final state is profitable, you keep the spread

• $0 loan outstanding • $0 profit • 0 blocks elapsed (it’s all inside one block-time action)
• “Repay now, or it never happened” is exactly why lenders don’t require collateral

Practical Takeaway: Flash loans remove the upfront capital barrier, but they punish mistakes instantly via full tx reverts. Always test for slippage, MEV, and repayment routing—one bad assumption can zero out the trade.

What’s more dangerous in flash-loan strategies: price impact/slippage or MEV/front-running? Comment your pick.

fb_caption:
Flash Loans (VIZ 13) are DeFi’s “atomic leverage” primitive: you borrow, execute, and repay within a single transaction—so there’s never any persistent loan exposure to the lender.

What happens on-chain (atomic mechanics):
- The transaction begins with a loan of a specified amount.
- Your contract performs arbitrary logic (DEX trades, arbitrage across pools, liquidation of positions, collateral swaps, etc.).
- The lender verifies repayment at the end of execution.
- If repayment is not satisfied, the EVM reverts the entire transaction: state changes from the attempt are rolled back.

Why it needs no collateral:
- Because repayment is enforced atomically. “Repay now, or it never happened” means the lender cannot end up holding an unpaid balance.
- In the animation: TRY #1 → REVERT → TRY #2 → PROFIT.
- At completion you observe $0 loan outstanding, because the loan is guaranteed to be repaid in the same transaction lifecycle.

Protocol trade-offs & security implications:
- Slippage & price movement: Even if the logic is correct, on-chain execution depends on real-time pool states. A small deviation can prevent profit > fees, triggering failure/revert.
- MEV risk: Arbitrage and liquidation routes can be front-run or sandwiched. Your tx may still execute, but the “profit” leg can be stolen or made unprofitable, causing reverts or negative outcomes.
- Execution complexity: A flash loan strategy is only as safe as its assumptions—route selection, token approvals, fee math, and insolvency edge cases.
- Reentrancy & callback surfaces: Many flash loan providers use callbacks (e.g., executeOperation). Contracts must be written defensively because they’re invoked with elevated privileges to move funds.

Tokenomics note (contextual):
- Flash loans aren’t typically “token-driven” by themselves, but they influence market conditions: price discrepancies get arbitraged away and liquidation activity can spike. This can affect protocol usage metrics that token incentives often target.

Security checklist for builders:
- Verify profit condition on-chain (not off-chain projections).
- Bound slippage with sensible minimum outputs.
- Consider MEV protection (private relays / bundling) and simulate with realistic state.
- Ensure repayment logic is deterministic and reachable in all paths.

Debate: In your view, should flash loans be more restricted by protocol risk controls—or should they remain open because the atomic revert model is already sufficient?
